title: OpenC910 (XUANTIE-RV/openc910)
_note: T-Head's XuanTie C910: the 64-bit RV64GCV out-of-order core (ifu / idu / iu /
lsu / rtu / mmu / cp0 / had), its vector-FP units (vfalu, vfdsu, vfmau, vfpu),
the L2 cache, the bus interface and coherency units, the CLINT / PLIC / PMP /
PMU, and the smart_run integration platform around it (AXI / AHB / APB
fabrics, UART, GPIO, timers).  The checked-in filelist
gen_rtl/filelists/C910_asic_rtl.fl is a flat list of 486 paths and needs no
generation -- no FuseSoC, no Bender, no mill.
cpu_cfig.h and sysmap.h hold nothing but `define`s and are never `include`d
by any file -- the filelist compiles them first -- so they go in always_srcs,
and the family must read --single-unit: compiled as its own unit each, a file
never sees the other's macros and read_slang stops at
`unknown macro or compiler directive '`PA_WIDTH'`, losing the REFERENCE for
every row that uses one.
gen_rtl/fpga/rtl is not an FPGA-only variant: it holds the 41 ct_f_spsram_*
models (and fpga_ram) that the ct_spsram_* wrappers in lsu/rtl instantiate
unconditionally, which is why they are in the ASIC filelist.  They are
always_srcs rather than rows -- a behavioural RAM is a library cell, and as
rows all 41 were unprovable (`SAT over memory cap` or `SAT timeout`, every
one with a clean co-simulation and 0 undriven).
First local sweep 2026-10-26 (482 rows, MEM_LIMIT_KB=7000000 as the nightly
uses): 346 / 481 comparable proven, 463 / 481 elaborate, 0 undriven on every
row that read, 356 co-sim PASS, 9.5 h of row time (hence eight shards).
Open: 113 rows exhaust the SAT budget (64 timeout, 49 over the memory cap) --
the whole-core rows ct_core / ct_top / openC910 / soc, the 10 ct_spsram_*
cache-RAM wrappers and the wide datapath blocks -- every one of them with a
clean co-simulation and 0 undriven, so they are budget rows, not defects.
The 11 rows that read-FAILED on that first sweep are CLOSED by #1350: all of
them reached ct_prio (the round-robin priority matrix) -- ct_prio itself,
ct_piu_top and nine ct_ciu_* -- whose concatenation LHS writes two unpacked
arrays' row i from a generate loop, and the concat path did not fold a genvar
element index, so the bare array name was reported and the whole read aborted
with `ERROR: Signal prio not found in module`.  Re-measured against the fix
all 11 read with 0 undriven: 9 are proven with a clean co-simulation and the
other 2 (ct_ciu_snb, ct_ciu_top) are SAT-budget rows.  That is 355 / 481
proven and 0 read-fails; test/varsel_concat_genvar_elem is the ratchet.
One divergence lead: plic_hreg_busif, `differs` with 5 slang-clean
co-simulated divergences.  axi2ahb's 274 divergences are NOT a reader
defect: read_slang refuses the module for unsynthesizable timing control, so
the row has no reference and the RTL side simulates delays the netlist
cannot have.  top_golden_port / mp_top_golden_port are empty monitor shells
(`Can't find gold module`), and ct_spsram_2048x88's `dumped core` is the
300 s timeout killing a miter mid-write, not a read failure -- it reads with
0 undriven and co-simulates clean.

axi2ahb.note: adjudicated 2026-10-29: the 274 co-sim divergences are a DELAY artefact, not a reader defect. axi2ahb drives its FSM through three DELAYED continuous assignments -- `assign #1 nxt_st_dly[8:0] = nxt_st[8:0];` (axi2ahb.v:318) plus readaxi_last_data (:477) and db_wr (:561). Verilator lowers `assign #1` to a NON-BLOCKING assignment, so the RTL's nxt_st_dly lags a delta; any synthesis netlist drops the delay and makes it combinational. read_slang refuses the file outright for the same construct (`unsynthesizable timing control`), which is why the row had no reference and no verdict. Mitered and co-simulated against the GOLDEN read_verilog netlist instead: it diverges at the SAME cycle on the SAME signal for the SAME count (FIRST-SLANG cycle 25 pad_biu_wready rtl=1 slang=0, slang_vs_rtl=274), so the harness reports SHARED_DIVERGENCE -- both frontends agree and the RTL's delay is the difference
